observation.visible_scene: A low-angle sunset view of a calm sea with the sun sitting on the horizon, casting a bright vertical reflection column on the water to the right. In the left foreground a clear glass sphere rests on a bed of wet, rounded pebbles at the shoreline; the sphere holds an inverted image of the scene (a curved horizon line and a bright vertical sun-reflection streak on its left side). The composition is otherwise static: sky, horizon, sun, sphere position, and pebble layout do not shift across the excerpt.
visible_changes: Small ripples and thin sheets of water repeatedly advance and retreat over the pebbles in the lower half of the frame, so the wet/dry boundary around the stones and around the base of the sphere changes shape from frame to frame.
The sun's reflection column on the open water shimmers: the distribution of bright patches and broken highlights within it changes over time while its overall vertical position stays the same.
The bright vertical sun-reflection streak inside the glass sphere flickers in shape and intensity, tracking the same surface motion seen in the external reflection.
The inverted horizon line and sky reflection within the sphere remain present throughout, with only minor internal shimmering.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the shoreline water is on an overall rising or falling wave cycle, since the excerpt is a temporally cropped segment with arbitrary endpoints.
Any longer-term tide or wind behavior beyond this window.
uncertain_details: Camera motion: background elements (sun, horizon, sphere, pebbles) hold fixed frame positions, so the camera appears static; only the water and reflections move.
The exact material of the sphere is not confirmable from the frames alone, though it behaves optically like a transparent refracting ball.
